archetype.name: Pocket Passer (aggressive)
archetype.definition: An 18-year veteran who wins from a clean pocket with timing and anticipation, built to push the ball into intermediate windows, and who has always accepted interceptions as the cost of throwing into tight coverage.

report.headline: League-leading yardage, middling efficiency, and now the Adams-shaped hole in the middle
report.take:
Stafford is the same quarterback he has been for a decade and a half: a rhythm passer who stays in the pocket, gets the ball out on time, and will fit throws into windows other quarterbacks pass up. The 2026 box score flatters him. He leads the league in passing yards and ranks second at 299 a game, but that comes from volume, at 41.5 attempts a game on a team that passes more than situations call for (7th in pass rate over expected). Judged per play, he sits 21st in EPA per dropback at 0.113. That is comfortably above the league average of 0.034, but it is a long way from last year's MVP-level line of 46 touchdowns and an EPA per play ranked 8th.

The season splits sharply by depth. Between 10 and 19 air yards he has been excellent: 0.43 EPA per attempt on 57 throws, the engine of the offense. Underneath he is accurate and efficient, completing 77.4% with a +4.1 CPOE. The deep ball has collapsed. He is 26.9% on 26 throws of 20+ yards with a -9.4 CPOE and three interceptions, and his aggressiveness is down 4 points from last year. At 38, that deserves attention, though 26 attempts is a small enough sample that a handful of near-misses can swing it. The other drags are third down (-0.144 EPA) and the check-downs to Kyren Williams (-0.102 EPA per target on 39 targets).

What the numbers hide is how much of this rested on one receiver. Davante Adams' targets added 22.1 EPA at 0.451 per target, which is more than all of Stafford's dropbacks combined (20.9). Puka Nacua has drawn more targets but turned them into far less, at 0.127 per target. Adams ruptured his hamstring against Arizona and is not expected back until around the Week 11 bye. That Arizona game, a two-point loss as 12.5-point favorites, already looked like an offense without a vertical answer: 4.8 intended air yards and a 3% aggressiveness rate, the lowest of his season by far.

The outlook from here is volume holding up and efficiency drifting down. Pass protection has been a real asset: he is pressured on only 13.3% of dropbacks (4th) and sacked at a 3.9% rate (7th). The short game is real. But without his best intermediate and contested-window target, the throws that drove his efficiency go to receivers who haven't produced on them. Expect plenty of 270-yard, one-touchdown afternoons until Adams returns.

strengths.title: Intermediate window throwing
strengths.body: His 10-to-19-yard throws have produced 0.43 EPA per attempt with nearly 58% success. This is the anticipation and arm talent that has defined his career, and it carried the offense through six games. The worry is that Adams caught a large part of that work, so the skill should last but the results may dip until he is back.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, few sacks
strengths.body: He has been pressured on 13.3% of dropbacks (4th) and sacked at a 3.9% rate, nearly 3 points under the league average. His pressure-to-sack rate (20.6%, 9th) carries on a trend from last season, when he ranked 8th. That points to quick processing behind a sound line rather than luck. His two worst games, SF and DEN, were the two in which he was pressured 25% or more, so this is the condition the whole offense depends on.

strengths.title: Accurate, efficient short game
strengths.body: On throws under 10 air yards he is completing 77.4% with a +4.1 CPOE on the 0-9 range and seven touchdowns against one interception. Tempo brings out his best: 0.459 EPA a play and a +15.4 CPOE in the no-huddle, though that is only 39 plays. This floor travels well, and it should matter more now that the downfield picture is thinner.

concerns.title: Losing his most productive target
concerns.body: Adams turned 49 targets into 22.1 EPA. The rest of the group has been far less efficient: Nacua at 0.127 per target, Mumpfield around zero and Williams negative. Adams is out until roughly late November after hamstring surgery. This isn't a flaw in Stafford, but it removes the receiver who made his aggressive throws pay off, and the first look at life without him produced a season-low air-yards game.

concerns.title: The deep ball has gone missing
concerns.body: On 20+ yard throws he is 26.9% complete with a -9.4 CPOE, three interceptions and negative EPA. His aggressiveness is down 4 points from last season. At his age, a real arm or confidence change can't be ruled out. But 26 attempts is a hint, not a verdict, and his career deep production argues this is partly noise.

concerns.title: Interceptions and third-down drag
concerns.body: His 2.4% interception rate ranks 32nd, and five of the six came on throws of 10+ air yards. That has been his profile for years, including 17 interceptions in 2021, so it is the price of the style more than a new problem. The fixable issue is third down, where his plays have produced -0.144 EPA despite a 40% conversion rate. Those empty third downs are a big reason the Rams are 2-4 while he leads the league in yards.

trend.note: His games swing between big performances (18.6 and 18.5 EPA against the Giants and Bills) and flat ones near or below zero (Denver, Philadelphia, Arizona). The last five games (0.149 EPA per dropback) beat his season number only because the Week 1 dud against San Francisco falls out of that window.

nextGame.headline: Raiders' leaky short defense fits him, if the pass rush doesn't
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas is close to an ideal opponent for an offense that has to lean on short timing throws. The Raiders are last in the league in EPA allowed on short passes (0.295) and 25th in pass EPA overall, and they allow 20.5 PPR a game to quarterbacks (27th). Their run defense is solid (8th in rush EPA), which should keep the Rams throwing, and their own passing offense ranks 5th in EPA, so a shootout script is plausible. The Book has the Rams as 4.5-point favorites with a 47.5 total. The catch is that Las Vegas hits quarterbacks at the 4th-highest rate in the league, and pressure is exactly what produced his two worst games.

Availability cuts both ways. Adams is out, so Nacua becomes the clear top receiver, and the Raiders have held WR1s 3.5 points under their averages (8th). The soft spot is their play against WR2s, last-tier in both points over average and EPA allowed, so whoever takes Adams' snaps could see the most open looks. Las Vegas is without DT Tonka Hemingway (concussion, 52% of snaps), which slightly eases the interior rush. The game is indoors.

keyMatchups.title: Short game vs worst short defense
keyMatchups.body: His 0-9 yard passing is accurate and efficient, and Las Vegas is 32nd against short throws. If Adams' absence pushes the offense underneath, as it did against Arizona, this is the defense to do it against. Expect a high completion rate.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' hit rate vs his pocket
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas ranks 4th in QB hit rate, while the Rams' line has allowed hits at a middling rate (16th). Stafford has thrived when kept clean and struggled when pressured 25% or more. Hemingway's absence helps at the margin.

keyMatchups.title: Who wins the WR2 opening
keyMatchups.body: The Raiders have been strong against top receivers but have given up 0.73 EPA a target to WR2s (31st). Without Adams, the production may flow to the second receiver and tight end Tyler Higbee (0.225 EPA per target) rather than Nacua. Las Vegas also sees an above-average share of targets go to tight ends.

nextGame.watch: Whether he still attacks 10-19 yards without Adams or settles into another sub-5-yard air-yards game like Week 6.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the stable part: a pass-leaning McVay offense, a team defense that is only average, and a quarterback who rarely takes sacks will keep him near 40 attempts a week. Expect efficiency to slip during the five weeks or so before Adams' expected return. The intermediate game that carried his EPA has relied on Adams, and the other targets haven't converted their looks at nearly the same rate. I'd project roughly 255-295 yards and 1.3-1.9 touchdowns a game in that stretch, with EPA per dropback closer to league-average-plus than to last year's level.

The deep-ball slump is the most likely number to improve, because 26 attempts is a thin sample for a passer with his history. The interception rate is the least likely to change, since it is who he has always been. If Adams comes back near full speed after the bye, the late-season version should look more like the Weeks 2-5 quarterback.
swingFactors: Adams' recovery timeline and form after surgery
Whether the deep ball regains accuracy
Pass protection holding against stronger rushes

confidence.note: Six-game sample, small deep-ball split, and a major role shift with Adams out.
